question: Which statement best describes container-type and container-name?
options: Container units are relative to the query container's size: cqw = 1% of container width, cqh = 1% of container height, cqi = 1% of the inline size, cqb = 1% of the block size, plus cqmin/cqmax. They let you size type and spacing relative to the component's box rather than the viewport — e.g. font-size: clamp(1rem, 5cqi, 2rem) makes text fluid to the container.

Media queries respond to the viewport (or device), which is global; container queries respond to a component's available space, which is local. A card in a wide main column and the same card in a narrow sidebar can look different from each other on the same screen — impossible with media queries alone. Container queries make components self-contained and reusable across layouts.

An element becomes a query container when you set container-type. container-type: inline-size lets descendants query its inline (usually width) dimension; size queries both dimensions but requires the container to have a defined size. container-name gives the container a label so a @container rule can target a specific named ancestor. The shorthand container: name / type sets both at once.

@container applies styles to descendants when the nearest matching query container satisfies a size condition, e.g. @container (min-width: 400px) { .card { display: flex; } }. You can target a named container with @container card (min-width: 400px). The condition is evaluated against the container's size, not the viewport — so the same component adapts wherever it's placed.

question: Which statement best describes @container queries?
options: Container units are relative to the query container's size: cqw = 1% of container width, cqh = 1% of container height, cqi = 1% of the inline size, cqb = 1% of the block size, plus cqmin/cqmax. Setting container-type also establishes layout/style/size containment on the element, which can affect how its own size is computed (notably size containment collapses intrinsic sizing of its contents). inline-size is the common, low-risk choice because it only contains in one axis. Importantly, an element cannot query ITSELF — only descendants can query an ancestor container.

question: Which statement best describes Container query units (cqw, cqi, cqh, cqb)?
options: Container queries are supported in all modern evergreen browsers (Chrome/Edge 105+, Firefox 110+, Safari 16+) as of recent versions. For older browsers, design a sensible default (often the stacked, single-column layout) so the component is usable without the @container enhancement, and optionally use @supports (container-type: inline-size) to scope progressive enhancements.
